questions: Do you have weakness in your legs that makes it difficult to lift the front of either foot while walking?
Did this weakness begin suddenly or worsen noticeably over days to weeks?
Does the weakness become worse with activity and improve after rest?
Have you had drooping of either eyelid?
Do you have difficulty speaking, chewing, or swallowing, especially later in the day?
Have you had shortness of breath when lying down or during routine activity?
Do you have numbness or tingling in your legs or feet?
Do you have back pain that radiates into either leg?
Have you had difficulty controlling your bladder or bowels?
Have you experienced episodes of vision loss, eye pain, or blurred vision?
Have you had similar neurological symptoms in the past that later improved?
Do you have weakness or clumsiness in your arms or hands?
Have you recently had an infection, diarrhea, or a vaccination before these symptoms began?
Do you have diabetes, thyroid disease, or any autoimmune disease?
results: 1. nerve conduction studies: demyelinating sensorimotor neuropathy
2. whole exome sequencing: heterozygous likely pathogenic FBLN5 c.1117C>T (p.Arg373Cys) - CMT1H
3. MRI brain with contrast: bilateral contrast enhancement and THICKENING of cranial nerves III through XII
4. MRI spine: symmetrical thickening of the lumbosacral nerve roots
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: FBLN5-related Charcot–Marie–Tooth disease type 1H (CMT1H), caused by the heterozygous pathogenic FBLN5 c.1117C>T (p.Arg373Cys) variant, with hypertrophic demyelinating cranial and lumbosacral polyradiculoneuropathy.

CIDP or another immune-mediated hypertrophic polyradiculoneuropathy

CMT1A due to PMP22 duplication

CMTX1 due to GJB1 mutation
dx: FBLN5-related Charcot–Marie–Tooth disease type 1H (CMT1H), caused by the heterozygous pathogenic FBLN5 c.1117C>T (p.Arg373Cys) variant, with hypertrophic demyelinating cranial and lumbosacral polyradiculoneuropathy.
